_doc: Readable notes of pool round 2 (random-town set pieces; no note names its town). Items: items/town4.json note_<id>.

defs.title: The Book on the Counter
defs.author: Ray Hollis
defs.body:
Day 2. 30-30 to the Pruett boy. Two .243s, the Remington pump, all the .22 LR on the shelf. Cash only, no layaway, sorry.
Day 3. Cordon by at noon with a list. Told them I'm a licensed dealer. They said that doesn't mean anything now.
Day 4. Grille down. Moved the counter stock to the vault room.
Day 5. Danny came in the alley door. Forearm. I promised his mother.
Day 5. Put him in the vault with the lamp and the radio and locked it. Going down to sit a while. Key's on me.

defs.title: Notice Taped to the Door
defs.author: Cordon Command
defs.body:
ORDER 14 — FIREARMS

All firearms and ammunition held for sale are to be surrendered to Cordon personnel. Licensed dealers will be issued receipts.
Premises refusing inspection will be sealed.

Under it, in marker: SEALED. DO NOT ENTER.

defs.title: Folded in the Desk Drawer
defs.author: Ray Hollis
defs.body: Danny — if you're reading this you got out, and I'm sorry. The vault key's with me downstairs. Don't come down. The rifles in the rack are loaded. Take the .30-06 and go north to your mother's. Don't come back for me.

defs.title: Tally Book
defs.author: Walt Kessler, foreman
defs.body:
Mon. 1,140 cases rations (beans/pork) to dock. QM counts every one.
Tue. 960. Two off sick. QM says sick go to the clinic, not home.
Wed. 410. Line stopped twice. Ortiz bit Lena on the belt and we all stood there.
Thu. Guards chained the office door from the street side. Told us keep packing.
Thu night. I'm up here with the spare cold-store key on its hook. QM's in the cold store with the stock and won't open. The line's still on the floor. They're still standing at the belts. I can hear them.

defs.title: Requisition Order
defs.author: Cordon Logistics
defs.body:
REQUISITION — FOOD PROCESSING FACILITY

This plant, its stock, vehicles and staff are placed under Cordon control for the duration. Production quota: 1,200 cases daily. Cold store under the Quartermaster's sole key.
Staff absent without leave will be treated as exposed.

defs.title: Pinned Inside the Cold Store
defs.author: Sgt. D. Mercer, Quartermaster
defs.body: Stock as of tonight: 2,214 cases. Signed for every one. Nobody is getting them without a signature. I've got the door and I've got the cold. If you're reading this you came in with Walt's key and I hope to God you're Cordon.

defs.title: Operator's Log
defs.author: Gus Lindqvist
defs.body:
Chlorine up to 4 ppm per Cordon. Tastes like a pool. Better than the alternative.
Crew sent home, all three coughing. Running it myself.
Day 9. Pressure holding. Half the town's drawing from the plant tap at the gate.
Day 11. Dale and Mikey came back. Nowhere else with clean water, they said. Put cots out in the pump hall. They're not right.
Day 12. Stores key's on the lab hook. The stores are for the town. Going down to count the tablets.

defs.title: Notice in the Front Hall
defs.author: Water Department
defs.body:
BOIL WATER NOTICE

By order of the Cordon all tap water is to be boiled for one full minute before drinking.
Emergency water and purification tablets will be issued at this plant to residents with ration cards.

Under it, in pencil: plant tap at the gate is still good - Gus

defs.title: Taped to a Store Shelf
defs.author: Gus Lindqvist
defs.body: Tablets 4,800. Jugs 312. Filters 40. For the town. Not for whoever gets here first. If you got here, you're the town now. Take what you need and leave the door how you found it.

defs.title: Scale Ticket
defs.author: Ridgeline Aggregate
defs.body:
SCALE TICKET 004417
GROSS 0 - TARE 0 - NET 0
MATERIAL: NONE
HAULER: CORDON

On the back, in pencil: roads closed. radio says stay put. Pete won't open the mag. manager's key is in his desk, top drawer, same as always.

defs.title: Seizure Order
defs.author: Cordon Engineering
defs.body:
NOTICE OF SEIZURE

All explosive materials, detonators and blasting equipment on these premises are seized for Cordon use under emergency regulation 6.
The licensee will surrender the magazine on presentation of this order.

Scrawled across it: NOT WITHOUT THE MANAGER'S SIGNATURE - P.H.

defs.title: Chalked Inside the Magazine
defs.author: Pete Haralson
defs.body:
Day 4. They can have it with Dale's signature. Dale's sick.
Day 6. Not opening.
Day 8. Cough. Ha.
(lower down, shakier) Don't light a match in here.

defs.title: Post Bulletin Board
defs.author: The Post Commander
defs.body:
NOTICE TO MEMBERS AND GUESTS
The hall is open to anyone who needs a roof. Cots by the stage, families by the windows.
Canteen is closed. Coffee is free.
NO ONE goes in the cellar. The quartermaster has the stores and he will issue them.
Thursday bingo is CANCELLED until further notice.

Pinned under it: FALL RAFFLE - presentation revolver - drawing postponed.

defs.title: Minutes of a Special Meeting
defs.author: Post Adjutant
defs.body:
Special meeting called to order 1900 hrs. 22 members present, 40-odd guests.
Motion: open the cellar stores to the guests. Seconded. Carried.
Quartermaster objected. Said the stores are counted and he will issue by the count, and the raffle revolver stays boxed until the drawing.
Motion: issue the raffle revolver to a member for the defence of the hall. Not seconded.
The commander asked the quartermaster for the cage key. He said it's in the till where it always is and he'll know if it moves.
Meeting adjourned 1940 hrs. Two guests in the hall reported sick.

defs.title: Inventory, Pencil on Cardboard
defs.author: The Quartermaster
defs.body:
Beans 6 cs. Peaches 4 cs. Coffee 2 cs. Blanks 300 (funeral detail).
Revolver .38, raffle, boxed: 1. Cartridges for same: 6 bx.
Night 5. They're coughing up there. I locked the cage. I'll issue by the count when it's over.
Night 6. Somebody tried the till. I heard the drawer.
(the last line goes off the edge) the count is the count
